title: P1 follow-on — pinned profiles and VM usability integration
objective: Deliver the next focused integration PR on feat/vm-useability-tweaks targeting feat/vm-approach-3. Coordinate independently reviewed workstreams for VM profiles, host metrics, terminal behavior, and public CLI/settings. PR #20 is merged and owner reports successful live VM use; retain honest provenance and outstanding defects. This is not Phase 1 completion, a general VM migration system, or the later in-VM cleanup PR. Owner decision (2026-11-24): named profiles may coexist with the original feat/vm-approach development VM, distinct from the fixed #20 singleton. Only the fixed singleton is mutually exclusive with profiles through four minimal manifest-owned additive systemd guards installed by the common signed control artifact and race-safe shared/exclusive admission lock; native package managers are dependency-only. Profile starts use actual host MemAvailable and bounded profile cgroups. Singleton guard retirement is deferred to #57 after its gates and explicit owner authorization.

acceptance_criteria.text: A shared public CLI grammar and profile-to-immutable-runtime-SHA contract is documented and consistently implemented across profile and CLI workstreams before implementation diverges.
Four focused workstream branches have independent tickets, tests, exact-candidate review, and are integrated from the common PR #20 base without changing feat/vm-approach-3.
The integrated candidate passes focused and full relevant local tests plus hosted CI; evidence records exact source SHA and run separately.

Owner validates profiles, workspace behavior, TUI keys, useful host metrics, ordinary settings, real provider auth/model response, persistence, and public acceptance on Ariadne; no report/test is claimed before supplied.
PR #20 remains merged; preserve the original feat/vm-approach VM as fallback; this integration does not start the later comprehensive cleanup PR or declare Phase 1 complete.

The integration contract and implementation distinguish the original feat/vm-approach development VM from the fixed #20 system singleton. The development VM remains usable concurrently with named profiles and receives no cap or lifecycle changes. Only the fixed singleton is temporarily mutually exclusive via four minimal manifest-owned additive guards installed by the common signed control artifact and a race-safe shared/exclusive admission lock; bootstrap requires either exact baseline interlocks on all four installed singleton units or all four singleton unit names absent (not masked), no pre-existing unit drop-ins, state or jobs, installing guards before later singleton installation; partial/masked states refuse. Blockers are actionable. Profile starts account for actual host MemAvailable, active profile cgroup headroom and configured caps. Identical owner-facing install/lifecycle commands work on supported Ubuntu, Debian, Arch and CachyOS hosts; native package managers are used for system dependencies only. Singleton retirement/guard removal is deferred to #57 after gates and explicit authorization.

Cross-workstream acceptance separately starts the original development VM with profiles and verifies coexistence, while simultaneous fixed-singleton/profile starts are mutually excluded and identify the blocking profile. Record actual host MemAvailable/resource tests and defer singleton retirement/removal to the authorized #57 cleanup.

Cross-stream regression proves the original development VM remains active and ungated while profile starts honor its actual memory use; profile admission also reserves active profiles’ unused cgroup headroom. Install the signed control package and verify fixed-singleton owner acceptance before/after it, with only the exact package-owned component guards accepted.

Cross-distribution regression uses identical ./lab vm bootstrap, control update, profile install and lifecycle commands on Ubuntu and CachyOS; signed helper/runtime manifests and generated systemd units match. Only host dependency setup differs via apt versus pacman; no native package manager installs or updates the control helper, guards or SHA runtimes.

Supersession for earlier evidence wording: “install the signed control package” means run the common signed, distribution-independent bootstrap artifact, not install a Debian/Arch package. Both system-acceptance and tools/vm-system-install update/rollback verifiers must accept only the manifest-owned four guards after bootstrap; native package managers are dependency-only.

Cross-stream regression verifies common bootstrap refuses without exact effective baseline code-update interlocks on all four fixed singleton units; both existing fixed-system verifier paths enforce strict exact baseline/manifest-bound sets and only transaction-owner recovery clears a matching typed marker.

Manifest terminology correction: the common control artifact and bootstrap executable are signed; each immutable SHA-runtime manifest is generated root-owned by the fixed helper from the exact committed Git tree and validated against its inventory/digests, not separately signed. Cross-distribution tests compare both trust/manifest paths without conflating them.

Cross-stream bootstrap tests cover both accepted host states: all four fixed units with exact baseline interlocks, or all four absent with no singleton state/jobs and four guards preinstalled for a later fixed-system install. Partial, masked or malformed states refuse.

Bootstrap-state wording supersession: an absent fixed singleton is accepted only if all four names are truly absent (not masked), with no pre-existing drop-ins, singleton state or queued jobs. An installed singleton requires exact 90 guards on all four units; partial/malformed installs refuse.

Distribution-scope correction: support is required on all four named host IDs—Ubuntu, Debian, Arch and CachyOS—not only the Ubuntu/CachyOS representatives. The existing adapter currently rejects Debian; add the explicit Debian→apt mapping and test the same prerequisite/lifecycle contract across all four. Unknown derivatives remain unsupported until reviewed.

Cross-stream regression covers initial bootstrap with absent config/group/code-update lock and transaction-safe idempotent substrate creation, plus the stopped unassigned singleton layout with no workspace 20 drop-in; both fixed verifiers enforce exact assignment/drop-in correspondence.

On Ariadne, record exact-SHA read-only deployed-candidate verification for d60e142d44a6c7b68464b4a3712bce635f99fb4f. Only after separate owner authorization, run lifecycle acceptance and record network boundaries, metrics transport/schema, direct-egress refusal, TUI exit, same-disk persistence, disk identity and final VM state; preserve the legacy development VM.

Capture direct live /metrics samples on the accepted fresh Ariadne install: source=host, stable run_id for the service process, at least two strictly advancing sequence/timestamp observations, and actual CPU/RAM/NVIDIA readings plus all availability codes. Treat optional-temperature no_sensors according to contract; do not infer live progression or accuracy from the one-sample automated transport check or visual TUI acceptance.
